headline: Waymo is weighing an end to its robotaxi partnership with Uber, and Uber's shares fell nearly 5% on the report.
score_reason: Significant for Uber's strategy, but rests on unnamed sources and a possible split dated to 2028.
importance_line: Riders in Austin and Atlanta could lose Waymo cars inside the Uber app from January 2028, and Uber's partner-based robotaxi plan looks shakier, though Waymo has decided nothing and the report relies on people familiar with the talks.
summary: The Financial Times reports, as relayed by Stocktwits, that Alphabet's Waymo has held internal talks about ending its robotaxi partnership with Uber and has told Uber it intends to run Austin and Atlanta on its own in January 2028, when the current agreement allows; Uber shares fell nearly 5% on 2 Oct 2026 after the report. The two companies increasingly compete head-on and have blamed each other over service quality and safety, and Uber has reportedly spent more than 10 billion dollars on autonomous-vehicle deals in the past year.
notes: Original FT reporting read via Stocktwits; FT link not available, url is the Stocktwits page. Stock move is part of the news (rule 5.4).
